newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Northwest sees drop in fish shipments.
newsitem.headline: Northwest sees drop in fish shipments.

text.p: Northwest Airlines has suffered a 26 per cent drop in fish shipments from Hong Kong to Japan, said the airline's general manager in Hong Kong, Gilbert Chow.

He blamed changing transport and economic patterns in the niche market.Chow said Northwest had enjoyed a lucrative fish trade for 20 years using the belly cargo space of Northwest's daily Boeing 747 flights to its Tokyo hub.

The morning flight and first of the day from Hong Kong to Tokyo had been popular for getting locally caught fish to the Japanese market early in the afternoon so it could be on the Sushi table that night, he added.
But various factors have caused the market to "dry up", Chow said.
One of the factors blamed are some fish exporters using wet sawdust instead of heavier ice to pack live seafood - the result is less tonnage and less revenue, he said.
"The same sized box with ice used to weigh 30 pounds now it's just 20 pounds," said Chow.
Another factor is increased spending power which means that more frozen fish is being bought in China, he said. In the past this would have been air freighted to Japan from Hong Kong.
Frozen fish is being transported overland, which can take three days by train or truck, to markets in Shanghai.

"It is a long way but until then the only choice in the past was to bring the fish from Shenzhen to Hong Kong. Now it is being transported north to Shanghai because the Chinese have more spending power and want more choice of fish to buy," said Northwest Cargo's manager sales and marketing Alexander Wong.
He said Osaka's newly-opened Kansai airport is also having an effect because it is offering more freighter capacity into Japan.
And the recent 20 per cent devaluation of the Japanese Yen has affected the buying power of Japanese consumers, Wong said.
"Fish is still an important market for us and the yield is quite good but it has been a bit disappointing this year and our bottom line has been affected," Wong said.
